dataFlow: When a shopper visits a sold-out product page, the widget queries Shopify Storefront for the variant's availability in real time and renders the sign-up form only when the item is unavailable; on submission the backend records a waitlist entry keyed by email + item scope and confirms inline. When inventory is updated, an inventory_levels/update webhook fires and the backend resolves the affected variant via inventoryItem admin query; if available quantity is now positive and no in-progress notification batch exists for that variant today, the backend creates a notification batch, selects the front-of-queue subscribers up to the configured notification quota, marks them as notified, and sends each a back-in-stock email respecting the merchant's configured quiet-hours window. When an order is paid, the backend checks its line items against recently notified waitlist entries for the same email within the 7-day attribution window and records a conversion. Merchants view the admin dashboard for waitlist rankings and drill-in, edit the message template, configure quiet hours and notification quota, and export subscriber lists as CSV; deleted products cascade-clear their waitlist rows via the products/delete webhook.

triggers.event: an inventory level is updated at a location
triggers.idempotency: if a notification batch for this variant was already created today (calendar day), treat as a no-op and do not create another batch; check stock state via live lookup at send time before each individual email

triggers.event: a product is deleted from the store
triggers.idempotency: deletion is idempotent — if no waitlist rows exist for the product, exit cleanly

signalFields: order line item variant external ids
triggers.idempotency: if conversion records already exist for this order external id, treat as a no-op

payloadBindings.signalField: order line item variant external ids

triggers.jobPurpose: Drain the pending notification queue by sending queued back-in-stock emails while enforcing quiet-hours and per-restock quota.
triggers.perTickWork: Fetch a batch of pending notification queue rows whose scheduled_after is in the past; for each row verify current stock via Shopify Admin, send the email if still in stock, and mark the row sent, failed, or skipped.

edgeCases: Duplicate inventory_levels/update delivery for the same variant on the same calendar day — the second event finds an existing notification batch record for that day and exits before enqueueing any sends or calling any external API.

Item sells out again between batch creation and the scheduled send tick — verify-stock-before-send returns unavailable and the notification queue row is marked skipped, not sent; the shopper is not emailed and remains on the waitlist for the next restock.

Restock occurs during the quiet-hours window — the queue row's scheduled_after is set to the start of the next active window so no email fires until quiet hours end even if the drain job ticks during silence.
Duplicate orders/paid delivery for the same order — the second delivery finds existing conversion rows keyed by order external id and exits as a no-op before writing any new records.
Shopper unsubscribes after being enqueued but before the drain tick fires — the drain job checks is_unsubscribed on the waitlist entry and marks the queue row skipped rather than sending.

Product is deleted while a notification batch is in progress — products/delete webhook triggers cascade delete of all waitlist entries, notification batch rows, and pending queue rows for that product; rows already marked sent are retained as historical records.

Email delivery fails with a provider bounce or timeout — the notification queue row is marked failed with the provider error as the failure reason; no automatic retry is attempted and the waitlist entry remains active for future restocks.

Shopper signs up at both product level and variant level for overlapping items — the two entries are independent scopes and each produces its own notification, so the shopper may receive two emails if both scopes restock independently.
